meta.title: Filter design as constrained optimisation
meta.tools: Weighted least-squares FIR design written as normal equations (own), equality-constrained LS via KKT system, comparison with scipy.signal.firls, trade-off curve by weight sweep
meta.summary: Formulate linear-phase FIR design as an explicit optimisation — minimise weighted squared error over pass- and stop-bands subject to exact constraints (unit DC gain, a forced null) — solve it in closed form via the KKT equations, and verify against SciPy and against the constraint values.
meta.problem: 'Design a low-pass filter' is vague. What exactly is being minimised, and how do hard requirements enter?
meta.theory:
Type-I amplitude A(ω) = Σ a_k cos kω is linear in a. Weighted LS: minimise $\int W(ω)(A(ω)-D(ω))^2dω ≈ \|W^{1/2}(Ca-d)\|^2$ ⇒ normal equations $C^TWCa = C^TWd$. Equality constraints Ea = f (e.g. A(0) = 1, A(ω_n) = 0) via
Lagrange multipliers: $\begin{bmatrix}C^TWC & E^T\\E&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}a\\λ\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}C^TWd\\f\end{bmatrix}$. Raising the stopband weight trades passband error for stopband energy along a convex curve.
meta.method: N = 51 taps (L = 25), passband 0–0.2, stopband 0.26–0.5 (cycles/sample), dense grid of 2000 points. Unconstrained WLS vs scipy.signal.firls; constrained version with A(0) = 1 exactly and a null at 0.3; weight sweep 1…1000.
